stem:
Aditya fills a small plastic cup with vinegar. He dips one aluminium strip and one copper strip into the vinegar so the strips do not touch, then joins both strips with wires to a small LED. The LED glows.

Which claims correctly judge this setup? One or more options may be correct.

options.text: It is a working Voltaic cell because the aluminium and copper strips are different metals in the vinegar electrolyte.
It is a working Voltaic cell because the glowing LED shows that a circuit can carry current from this cell.
It is a working Voltaic cell even if both strips were copper.
It is a working electromagnet because the LED glows.

teacher.key_rationale: A Voltaic cell needs two different metal electrodes and an electrolyte; aluminium and copper in vinegar meet that test, and the glowing LED shows current. Same-metal electrodes omit the different-metal condition; calling it an electromagnet swaps the term.
